body_excerpt: C++ language server now auto-configures MSBuild builds - GitHub Changelog Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app See what's new Search Changelog Docs Customer stories See what's new Try GitHub Copilot app Back to changelog Improvement November 10, 2026 • 2 minute read C++ language server now auto-configures MSBuild builds Table of Contents What changed Configure other build systems Get started Menu. Currently selected: What changed What changed Configure other build systems Get started The Microsoft C++ Language Server for GitHub Copilot CLI now bundles its MSBuild compile commands extractor and invokes it automatically. An agent no longer needs to discover and run a separate configuration skill before it can get precise code intelligence for your project. For more information, including the installation instructions, see the main repository page . What changed Previously, setting up go-to-definition, find references, and other language server features for an MSBuild-based C++ project required you to either provide your own compile_commands.json file or Copilot to locate and run a configuration skill before it could generate a compilation database. That extra discovery step added setup time and consumed tokens before Copilot could start working with your code. Now: The compile commands extractor is bundled directly with the C++ language server, so it’s always available. Copilot invokes the extractor when starting the language server on project open, with no manual or agent-driven setup skill required. Compilation database generation for MSBuild projects is deterministic, reducing setup token usage. Currently selected: Availability in GitHub Copilot Availability in GitHub Copilot Enabling access Learn more Share your feedback Gemini 4 Carbon, Google’s latest model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for complex coding, agentic, and reasoning tasks, with a focus on secure code generation and security-focused work. This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details. Availability in GitHub Copilot Gemini 4 Carbon is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. You can select the model in the model picker in: Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Copilot CLI GitHub Copilot coding agent GitHub Copilot app github.com GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android JetBrains IDEs Xcode Eclipse Rollout will be gradual. Check back soon if you don’t see it yet. Enabling access Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can manage access to Gemini 4 Carbon through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default model enablement, new models are automatically enabled unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disables this model. Learn more To explore all models available in GitHub Copilot, see our documentation on models and get started with Copilot. Share your feedback Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback.
